title: Highest temperature in London on September 8?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model runs from the Met Office and ECMWF indicate persistent cloud cover and periods of rain across London on September 8, limiting daytime heating and keeping the maximum temperature near 19–20°C. Westerly flow advects cooler maritime air while moderate winds enhance mixing, preventing stronger surface warming. Ensemble spread arises mainly from differences in cloud thickness and precipitation timing, which directly affect net solar radiation reaching the ground. Traders assign the highest implied probabilities to 19°C and 20°C because these align with the central tendency of short-range guidance, while lower odds on 21°C or 18°C reflect the modest chance of partial clearing or heavier rain suppressing the peak further. Updated model runs and observational data later today will refine these thresholds ahead of market resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Paris-Le Bourget Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=lfpb

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from GFS and other models indicate a high near 24–25°C for Paris on September 8, driven by an incoming Atlantic disturbance that increases cloud cover, southwesterly winds, and widespread showers or rain after a warmer September 7. This frontal passage lowers daytime maxima below recent norms while limiting solar heating, aligning with the market’s leading implied probabilities for 24°C and 25°C. Historical September averages near 22.6°C provide context, but the near-term model consensus and expected precipitation timing favor these mid-20s outcomes over warmer or cooler extremes. Updated model runs and official Météo-France guidance remain key variables ahead of resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather prediction models from sources including the GFS and JMA indicate a daytime high near 28–30°C for Tokyo on September 8, driven by southerly flow advecting warm, humid air under persistent cloud cover and scattered showers that limit solar heating. This setup aligns with early-September climatology while the 50–70% rain probability caps extremes, positioning 29°C as the modal outcome followed closely by 28°C and 30°C in trader pricing. Afternoon dew points near 24–26°C and light southerly winds further constrain peak readings, with any brief clearing potentially allowing brief spikes toward 30°C before renewed moisture arrives. Updated model runs overnight will refine the exact maximum ahead of resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Toronto Pearson Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=cyyz

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from Environment Canada, GFS, and other sources indicate a maximum temperature in Toronto on September 8, 2026, centered around 23–24°C under partly to mostly cloudy skies with light southerly or easterly winds and minimal precipitation risk.** This aligns closely with the historical average high of 23.5°C for the date and supports the market’s heavy weighting toward 24°C (50.5%) and 25°C (33.5%), which together capture over 80% of implied probability.

Recent model runs show little day-to-day shift, with highs projected near 22–24°C across multiple providers (e.g., 72–75°F conversions), reflecting stable late-summer conditions without strong warm or cold advection. Minor upside risk to 25–26°C exists if afternoon clearing or slightly warmer boundary-layer air materializes, consistent with the 8% probability on 26°C, while cooler outcomes below 23°C remain low-probability given the current guidance. Traders are effectively pricing the most likely range from the latest official and ensemble forecasts, with resolution depending on the official observed daily maximum.
